spec.title: Acknowledged (k6 202) vs rows inserted by the consumer, per second
spec.description: Blue line: events the API acknowledged. Orange line: rows the consumer inserted. During the outage the orange line is 0. After the restart look at how much is inserted and for how long. Under 'earliest' the second burst is smaller than the backlog the group lag shows. Under 'latest' there is almost no burst. Surprising: a burst as large as the lag. k6 series are not marked stale after a run, so the last value can linger for minutes.

spec.title: Group lag as Kafka reports it vs records that can still be read
spec.description: Lag (kafka_consumergroup_lag) is log end minus committed offset. It also counts records that retention already deleted. 'Readable' is log end minus log start: what is really still in the topic. Once the log start passes the committed offset, lag is bigger than readable, and the difference is the data that is gone. After the restart, 'earliest' brings lag to 0, 'latest' may leave the lag stuck: the consumer jumps to the end but commits nothing until it processes a chunk. Needs ep-kafka-exporter.

spec.legendFormat: readable records in topic (end - log start)

spec.title: API latency p50 / p99 (k6)
spec.description: The API does not talk to the consumer, so latency should not change when the consumer stops or restarts. Surprising: any step at t=15 s or at the restart. Native histogram form (the inventory has no _bucket series).

spec.title: Consumer group members
spec.description: 1 while a consumer runs, 0 during the outage. The group still exists with its committed offsets while it is empty (offsets are kept for offsets.retention.minutes, 7 days by default).

spec.title: Log start offset (oldest) per partition
spec.description: The first offset still in the partition. It jumps up when the broker deletes an expired segment. Steps appear only at the broker's retention check (every 5 min) and only for closed segments (segment.ms = 20 s). Surprising: smooth growth (retention is not a smooth process).

spec.title: Committed offset of the group per partition
spec.description: Where the group would continue. Frozen from the moment the consumer stops (t=15 s). Compare with the panel on the left: when the log start line of a partition goes above this line, the records between them are gone. After the restart it moves again (to the log start under 'earliest', not at all under 'latest' until a chunk is processed).

spec.title: Records deleted before anyone read them
spec.description: Sum over partitions of max(log start - committed, 0). This is the loss caused by retention alone. It must be 0 in the control and positive in earliest and latest. The run.sh audit prints the same number from kafka-get-offsets just before the restart.

spec.title: Consumer: records consumed per second
spec.description: ep_consumer_messages_consumed_total of the sink (a new process after the restart, so the counter restarts at 0 and rate() handles it). 0 during the outage. After the restart, a burst while it reads what is left (earliest) or nothing (latest).

spec.title: Run phase (ep_k11_phase)
spec.description: 0 consumer running, 1 consumer stopped, 2 consumer restarted, -1 no run. Written by run.sh into the node_exporter textfile directory. It exists in Prometheus only after the first run (ADDED BY K11). Use it to see where the outage starts and ends.

spec.title: CPU of the API and the consumer process
spec.description: One core is 1.0. The consumer line is missing during the outage (no process). Surprising: the consumer at its limit after the restart for a long time (the backlog read is then CPU bound, not Kafka bound).

spec.title: Host CPU busy: pinned core groups
spec.description: node_exporter, non-idle share of the pinned cores. Retention deletion and segment rolling are cheap, so a visible change at the broker checks would be surprising.

spec.title: k6 dropped iterations (must be 0)
spec.description: Must stay 0: the load generator kept the planned rate. A run with dropped iterations is discarded.

spec.title: k6 requests that were not 202
spec.description: Must stay 0. Any 503 or timeout means an event was not acknowledged and is not part of the audit.

spec.title: Generator CPU busy (keep below 70%)
spec.description: Non-idle share of the cores k6 is pinned to. Above about 70% the generator may be the limit.

spec.title: API event-loop delay p99
spec.description: eventpulse_event_loop_delay_seconds of the API. Should stay in the low milliseconds at 1000 req/s.

spec.title: Under-replicated partitions of the topic
spec.description: Must stay 0: all brokers stay up in this experiment. Anything else means the run was disturbed.

spec.title: Postgres pool waiting (consumer)
spec.description: Callers waiting for a Postgres connection in the consumer. Should be about 0: the restart backlog should not be limited by the pool.

spec.title: 1. The verdict: what was acknowledged and what reached Postgres
2. The mechanism: log start overtakes the committed offset
